findings.text: [A]: the purple blotches on the pale moon read as spots or bruises at night size, so the moon looks a little sick rather than friendly.
[B]: a soft glowing crescent holding a 3 on near-black is a calm night-light picture, but the tile is so dark it almost sinks into the dimmed home screen.
[C]: the big 6 under a dark hill with only a sliver of orange sun feels like dusk turning to dark, more lonely than cozy, and nothing in it twinkles.
[D]: stars, a smiling crescent and purple hills over a white page make a little picture-book bedtime scene, the warmest and brightest tile in the row; the 4 is tiny though.
[D]: the name cuts off to 'Paint by Mo...' under the icon, so the moonlight part of the name, the part a child would say, is lost.
All four are dark tiles on a dark screen; only [D] carries enough light and color to be found again at bedtime.
